options.description: I start the remote-control investigation immediately (read-only, no gate needed), report what actually broke, then ask 3-6 sharp questions before building the boot automation.
options.label: Diagnose now, then light grill (Recommended)

options.description: Diagnose, then design and build the auto-resume tool using my own judgment on every fork. Fastest, but I'll be picking the concurrency and auto-resume policy for you.
options.label: Straight through both

options.description: 12-18 questions across 3+ rounds covering both parts before any work, including the CONTEXT.md checkpoint. Heavier than I think this needs.
options.label: Full grill first (/grill-with-docs)

options.description: Investigate the phone/remote-control failure and stop there. No boot automation this session.
options.label: Diagnosis only

You can now continue with these answers in mind.

options.description: Runs `claude --resume <id> --remote-control "<title>"` per repo. Full history loaded, phone link live under the right name, ready to type. Sessions sit idle until you prompt them — resuming does not make Claude act.
options.label: Resumed + RC named (Recommended)

options.description: Full history loaded locally, no bridge registration. You run /remote-control yourself when you actually want the phone. Fewer moving parts, no server-side session churn.
options.label: Resumed, Remote Control off

options.description: Opens a Windows Terminal tab per repo, cd'd in, with the exact `claude --resume <id> --remote-control "<title>"` command pre-typed but NOT executed. You press Enter on the ones you want. Safest.
options.label: Terminal parked, not resumed

questions.question: What state should each restored session be in when you sit down?

options.description: A small JSON file naming the repos to restore. Explicit, predictable, survives you finishing a piece of work. I'd seed it with AlgoTrader, Masterpager, Millwright — today's three.
options.label: Pinned list I maintain (Recommended)

options.description: Scans ~/.claude/projects/ and restores the most recent conversation in each real project dir. Zero maintenance, but it will resurrect repos you're done with, and I'd have to exclude scratchpad/worktree dirs by rule.
options.label: Auto: newest session per repo

options.description: Restores the 3-4 most recently touched conversations regardless of repo. Follows what you actually worked on last, but the set silently changes day to day.
options.label: Auto: N most recent overall

options.description: Scheduled task at logon does it automatically, AND a desktop shortcut so you can re-run it any time (after a crash, or to add a repo back). The button also gives you a way to test it without rebooting.
options.label: Both: logon task + a button (Recommended)

options.description: Fully automatic on every login. Nothing to click, but also no easy way to re-run it mid-day.
options.label: Logon task only

options.description: One double-click each morning after you log in. Simplest to reason about and to disable; you stay in control of when sessions start.
options.label: Desktop button only

options.description: You type your password, then the sessions come up on their own. Keeps disk encryption and your account credential intact — this machine reaches production Postgres and holds exchange credentials.
options.label: No, I'll keep logging in (Recommended)

options.description: PC boots straight to desktop, sessions restore, zero touch. Requires storing your account password in the registry (or a Sysinternals Autologon LSA secret). Anyone with physical access is then inside your session.
options.label: Yes, configure Windows auto-login

options.description: Leave login manual, but let me look at whether the PC can be powered on remotely from your phone so it is already booted and logged in by the time you reach it. Investigation, not a build.
options.label: Wake-on-LAN instead

questions.question: Should I also remove the manual Windows login from your morning?

options.description: I answer the auto-rename question with research, move the tool into MM-toolbox with dynamic discovery, wire the installer, sync the skills per your choice below, and commit+push. I check in only if the skills diff turns up something I shouldn't decide alone.
options.label: Proceed on my judgment (Recommended)

options.description: I do the read-only investigation (upstream identity, what actually changed, whether auto-rename is even possible) and come back with 3-4 sharper questions before building or pushing anything.
options.label: Light-touch: a few more questions first

options.description: Tool into MM-toolbox + installer + dynamic discovery + push this session. The Matt Pocock skills sync becomes its own follow-up so a large upstream diff doesn't get rushed alongside a refactor.
options.label: Split it: build now, skills sync separately

questions.question: How do you want to run this block of work?

options.description: I identify upstream, fetch it, and produce a per-skill verdict: unchanged / upstream-only changes (safe to take) / touches your local adaptations (needs a call). Nothing is overwritten until you say so. Slowest to land, zero risk of losing your work.
options.label: Report the diff, I decide per skill (Recommended)

options.description: I take upstream wholesale for skills with no local edits, and three-way merge the rest, hard-excluding spawn-claude-session and anything the two 'generalize/project-agnostic' commits touched. Faster; I make the merge calls.
options.label: Auto-merge, protect known-local skills

options.description: Overwrite every vendored skill with the current upstream version. Simplest and cleanest lineage, but discards the AlgoTrader-generalization work and any other local edits.
options.label: Take upstream wholesale

questions.question: The vendored skills carry local adaptations. How should an upstream update treat them?

options.description: Any directory with a real conversation touched in the last N days (default ~14). Hard-excludes temp/scratchpad dirs, .claude/worktrees copies, and the home directory. Fully dynamic, no list to maintain, and the exclusions are rules rather than a pinned list.
options.label: Auto-discover, with exclusions + a recency window (Recommended)

options.description: Same discovery, but a newly-seen directory is listed as 'pending' and skipped until you approve it once. Safest against surprise restores; costs you one click per new project.
options.label: Auto-discover, but new repos need one confirmation

options.description: Every project directory that has a real conversation, however old. Maximum coverage; will resurrect long-finished work and open a lot of tabs.
options.label: Auto-discover everything, no window
